::: {.en}

## [How the states compare]{.en}[各州对比]{.zh}

::: {.en}
**Table B1. Victoria against NSW, WA, QLD and SA (levies 2026–27 unless stated)**

::: tw
| Dimension | VIC | NSW | WA | QLD | SA (and ACT, TAS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Thermal WtE policy | 2.5 Mt/yr cap, 94% allocated \[1, 30\] | Designated precincts only: Parkes, Southern Goulburn–Mulwaree, West Lithgow; Tomago proposed \[113\] | Permitted; the only state with large plants built \[45\] | Prefers waste-to-fuels; A\$45m budget support \[45\] | SA: no large project; ACT bans thermal WtE \[45\] |
| Landfill levy (metro / regional) | A\$177.19 / A\$88.42 \[4\] | A\$180.20 / A\$103.80; parts of southern NSW pay none \[114\] | About A\$90 (Perth) \[115\] [to verify]{.verify} | A\$125 (2025–26), rising to A\$165 by 2029–30 \[116\] | SA A\$171 / A\$85.50; ACT domestic gate fee A\$121.75 incl. GST; TAS A\$70.50 \[26, 45\] |
| Household sorting | Four bins; deadline 1 Jul 2027 (not yet legislated); FOGO for all households by 2030 \[34, 35\] | FOGO for households by 2030; large food-waste generators from July 2026 \[114\] | FOGO rollout in Perth and Peel [to verify]{.verify} | Council-led [to verify]{.verify} | Three bins common [to verify]{.verify} |
| Red-bin energy (assumed service) | 9.6–12.4 MJ/kg by council \[26\] | About 10.9 MJ/kg (garden bin assumed) \[26, 76\] | — | — | About 10.9 MJ/kg (garden bin assumed) |
| Waste generated | 15.7 Mt (2024–25) \[28\] | 21.4 Mt (2023–24), 66% recycled \[117\] | 7.4 Mt (2023–24), 65% recycled \[117\] | 9.81 Mt (2023–24), 57.1% recovered \[117\] | — |
| Projects | 7 cap licences; Maryvale approved (Appendix A) | Parkes (Cleanaway, Tadweer, Tribe) \[96\]; Woodlawn under assessment \[99\] | Kwinana operating; East Rockingham in receivership (Table 6) | Swanbank withdrawn in 2022 \[100\] | — |
| Read for CDEG | **Lead market** | Second market; Sydney waste can reach a Latrobe site only by rail, at about A\$103/t \[26\] | Commissioning or O&M for distressed assets | Fastest-rising levy | Small; Adelaide reachable by rail (Model 3) |
:::

**Why sorting matters for the furnace.** The more food a state takes out of the red bin, the richer and smaller its residual stream becomes (3.3). Victoria and NSW both mandate FOGO by 2030, so residual waste in the two largest markets will move towards the top of CDEG's grate window over a plant's life.
:::

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 填埋税（大都市/地区） | 177.19 / 88.42澳元 \[4\] | 180.20 / 103.80澳元；新州南部部分地区不征收 \[114\] | 约90澳元（珀斯）\[115\] [待核实]{.verify} | 125澳元（2025–26年），2029–30年升至165澳元 \[116\] | 南澳171 / 85.50澳元；首都领地生活垃圾处理费121.75澳元（含GST）；塔州70.50澳元 \[26, 45\] |
| 家庭垃圾分类 | 四桶分类；截止日期2027年7月1日（尚未立法）；2030年前所有家庭实行FOGO \[34, 35\] | 2030年前家庭实行FOGO；大型厨余产生单位自2026年7月起 \[114\] | 珀斯和皮尔地区推行FOGO [待核实]{.verify} | 由市政主导 [待核实]{.verify} | 三桶分类较普遍 [待核实]{.verify} |
| 红桶垃圾热值（假设的服务类型） | 各市政9.6–12.4兆焦/千克 \[26\] | 约10.9兆焦/千克（假设有园林垃圾桶）\[26, 76\] | — | — | 约10.9兆焦/千克（假设有园林垃圾桶） |

**分类为何影响焚烧炉：** 一个州从红桶中分出的厨余越多，其剩余垃圾的热值就越高、量就越少（3.3）。维州和新州都要求在2030年前实行FOGO，因此在两个最大的市场，剩余垃圾的热值在电厂寿命期内将逐步移向集团炉排适应范围的上端。
:::
